Op vrijdag 23 mei 2014 13:37:17 UTC+2 schreef Thomas Lin Pedersen:

> Hi All
>
> I'm happy to announce the availability of my new shiny extension package 'shinyFiles'.
>
> The purpose of the package is to make a server side file navigator available to shiny app developers, comparable to the given with the fileInput() function. The use cases are mostly the following:
> When an app is intended to run locally, the use of fileInput gives an unnecessary overhead by requiring selected files to be copied to a temporary location before being made available to the server script. This is of little concern with small files, but as the file sizes approach the Gb range it gets unacceptable. shinyFiles solves this by directly exposing the file system and making the full path of selected files available without copying.
> In some circumstances It might make sense to expose a subset of the server file system to the user in remote running apps (selecting old results or configuration files etc.). shinyFiles allow the developer to restrict the client access to a certain subdirectory of the full file system, by specifying a starting root, beyond which the client have no access. Furthermore subdirectories of the root can be removed as well as file-types to give fine-grained control over what is exposed to the client.
> The functionality is designed to be extremely simple to implement, and makes it easy to toggle between fileInput and shinyFiles. If you're designing your html from scratch it only requires the addition of a single <button> element to make it work.
>
> The visual side is designed to look great on bootstrap pages, but can be customised to your own needs. Furthermore the icons can be customised if you have your own icon set...
>
> At the moment it is only available on github (use devtools to install), but it should be submitted to cran after some further testing. After installation you can run shinyFilesExample() to be presented with a minimal app showing the functionality.
>
> I would welcome any feedback.
>
> best

> Thomas

messages.body_plain:
<https://lh4.googleusercontent.com/-x5BQPkDysq0/U4IgdCN5vjI/AAAAAAAAAKM/PyYcRv6Bb7Q/s1600/Example.png>
Dear all,

I recently came across the ReporteRs package, see here  <http://davidgohel.github.io/ReporteRs/index.html>and here  <https://github.com/davidgohel/ReporteRs>and it's pretty nice! It allows you to construct rich Word, PPT and HTML documents via R. Especially the table (FlexTable) capabilities are welcome to construct complex tables with dynamic styling. Since version 0.5.4 it allows you to extract the html of such tables, which means you can hook them up in your Shiny applications.

Obviously other table construction options exist, notably the datatable option, see here <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/datatables-options.html>. The latter, however, makes styling your table a little tedious. Another option is shiny-handsontable <https://github.com/wch/shiny-handsontable> .

To demonstrate the combination of ReporteRs  and Shiny I made a small toy app to show some capabilities. The main idea is that it will allow you to construct complex slice & dice applications, which results can be exported to a number of useful outputs i.e. PPT, Word, HTML. Another cool thing is that you can use preset style sheets and fill in results on the fly (via bookmarks, see here <http://davidgohel.github.io/ReporteRs/word.html>).

The toy example below allows you to pick a dataset, apply some silly formatting (e.g. color all cells with value x  > 50 in column y to green), store the results and export the report as a Word document. The shiny example is obviously very limited, it is only intended to illustrate how various elements can be combined. All credits for the package go to David Gohel.

In order to run the shiny example you need the ReporteRs package, version >= 0.5.4, which you can get here:

if( !require( devtools ) ) install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github('ReporteRsjars', 'davidgohel')
devtools::install_github('ReporteRs', 'davidgohel')

Below the ui.r and server.r scripts for the toy example. The added screen-shot gives a first impression.

kind regards, Herman Sontrop

###
### ui.r
###

library(ReporteRs)
library(shiny)

#modified action button, see https://gist.github.com/xiaodaigh/7012930
actionButton <- function(inputId, label, btn.style = "" , css.class = "") {
  if ( btn.style %in% c("primary","info","success","warning","danger","inverse","link")) {
    btn.css.class <- paste("btn",btn.style,sep="-")
  } else btn.css.class = ""
  tags$button(id=inputId, type="button", class=paste("btn action-button",btn.css.class,css.class,collapse=" "), label)
}

shinyUI(

  navbarPage( "Shiny interactive report",

    tabPanel("Table", icon = icon("table"),

      fluidRow(
        column(2,

              uiOutput("DatasetSelector"),
              uiOutput("ColumnSelector"),
              uiOutput("ColumnAlignment"),
              uiOutput("HeaderColor"),
              uiOutput("BorderColor"),
              uiOutput("HighlightColor"),
              uiOutput("MinNrOfEntries"),
              uiOutput("TextSize"),
              br(),
              actionButton("AddToWordReport","store table","primary",c("btn-xs")),
              actionButton("GenerateWordReport","generate report","primary",c("btn-xs")),
              h6("tables currently stored"),
              h1(textOutput("TableCount"))
        ),

        column(10,
              absolutePanel(htmlOutput("FlexTableExample"), draggable = TRUE)

        )

      )
    )
  )
)

###
### server.r
###

library(shiny)
library(ReporteRs)
library(datasets)

shinyServer(

  function(input, output, session){

    #some data sets to choose from
    datasetInput <- reactive({
      switch(input$mDataSet,
             "rock" = rock,
             "pressure" = pressure,
             "cars" = mtcars)
    })

    output$DatasetSelector <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('mDataSet',
                     label    = "select a dataset" ,
                     choices  =  c("rock", "pressure", "cars"),
                     multiple = FALSE,
                     selected = "cars")
    })

    output$MinNrOfEntries <- renderUI({

      mRange <- range(datasetInput()[,input$FlexColumn])
      mMid   <- floor(mean(mRange))

      sliderInput("MinNr", paste("Highlight records in", input$FlexColumn, "larger than"),
                  min = floor(mRange[1]), max = ceiling(mRange[2]), value = mMid, step = 1, ticks = FALSE)
    })

    output$ColumnSelector <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('FlexColumn',
                     label    = "select a column" ,
                     choices  = names(datasetInput()),
                     multiple = FALSE)
    })

    output$ColumnAlignment <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('mTextAlign',
                     label    = "text alignment" ,
                     choices  = c("left","center","right","justify"),
                     multiple = FALSE,
                     selected = "left")
    })

    output$TextSize <- renderUI({

      sliderInput("mTextSize", "text size",
                  min = 1, max = 50, value = 15, step = 1, ticks = TRUE)
    })

    output$HeaderColor <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('mHeaderColor',
                     label    = "header color" ,
                     choices  = colors(),
                     multiple = FALSE,
                     selected = "limegreen")
    })

    output$HighlightColor <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('mHighlightColor',
                     label    = "highlight color" ,
                     choices  = colors(),
                     multiple = FALSE,
                     selected = "purple2")
    })

    output$BorderColor <- renderUI({

      selectizeInput('mBorderColor',
                     label    = "border color" ,
                     choices  = colors(),
                     multiple = FALSE,
                     selected = "royalblue")
    })

    #construct a reative FlexTable object
    myFlexTable <- reactive({

      # set text size
      options( "ReporteRs-fontsize" = input$mTextSize )

      # construct a FlexTable with data.frame mtcars, display rownames
      myFlexTable = FlexTable(   data = datasetInput(),
                               , header.cell.props=cellProperties(background.color= input$mHeaderColor)
                               , header.text.props=textBold( color="white")
                               , add.rownames=TRUE
                               , body.par.props = parProperties(text.align = input$mTextAlign)
      )

      # give table zebra striped look
      myFlexTable = setZebraStyle( myFlexTable, odd = "#CCCCCC", even = "#F5F5F5" )

      # add border
      whiteBorder = borderProperties( color = input$mBorderColor )
      myFlexTable = setFlexTableBorders( myFlexTable
                                         , inner.vertical = whiteBorder, inner.horizontal = whiteBorder
                                         , outer.vertical = whiteBorder, outer.horizontal = whiteBorder
      )

      # mark cells above a threshold red
      Mark <- datasetInput()[,input$FlexColumn] > input$MinNr
      myFlexTable[Mark,input$FlexColumn] = cellProperties(background.color= input$mHighlightColor)

      # add footer
      myFlexTable = addFooterRow( myFlexTable, , value = "constructed with Shiny and ReporteRs"
                                  , colspan = ncol(datasetInput())+1, text.properties = textItalic(),
                                  par.properties = parProperties(text.alig = "center")

      )

      return(myFlexTable)

    })

    output$FlexTableExample <- renderUI({

      # extract HTML of the FlexTable
      x <- as.html(myFlexTable())

      #return result in div with class "shiny-html-output"
      return(div(HTML(x), class = "shiny-html-output"))

    })

    # maintain a list of FlexTable object such that we can print and modify them later
    FlexTableLog <- reactiveValues(
      mFlexTables    = list(),
      NrOfFlexTables = 0
    )

    #add FlexTable to log when action button is pressed
    observe({

      if(input$AddToWordReport == 0) return()
        CurrentLog   <- isolate(FlexTableLog$mFlexTables)
        NewFlexTable <- list(isolate(myFlexTable()))

      FlexTableLog$mFlexTables    <- c(CurrentLog,NewFlexTable)
      FlexTableLog$NrOfFlexTables <- isolate(FlexTableLog$NrOfFlexTables) + 1

    })

    observe({

      # take a dependency on WriteReport action button
      if(input$GenerateWordReport == 0) return()

      # construct a an empty docx object
      doc = docx()

      # in order to write text we need to specify a style
      # inspect which styles we have (note this depends on your language settings and Word version installed)
      print(styles(doc))

      # inform the doc object which styles we have
      doc = declareTitlesStyles(doc, stylenames = styles(doc))

      # as the shiny app doesn't know your system a priori we simply
      # pick a style by index e.g. 25 instead of by name
      StyleIndex <- min(25,length(styles(doc)))

      # add a title
      doc = addTitle( doc, "Shiny report", StyleIndex )

      #insert all FlexTables to doc object
      NrOfFlexTables <- isolate(FlexTableLog$NrOfFlexTables)

      for( i in 1:NrOfFlexTables){

        # make some room by adding an empty line
        # stylename: we need to use a valid style here
        doc = addParagraph(doc,"\n", stylename = styles(doc)[1])

        # extract table from log
        NewTable <- isolate(FlexTableLog$mFlexTables[[i]])

        # update the body font to a smaller size
        NewTable[,] =  textProperties(font.size = 8)

        # add table to doc object
        addFlexTable(doc,NewTable)
      }

      # construct a word document based on the constructed doc object
      writeDoc( doc,"Report.docx")

      # open result
      browseURL("Report.docx")
    })

    #display number of tables stored
    output$TableCount <- renderText(
      FlexTableLog$NrOfFlexTables
    )

  }
)

messages.body_plain:
<https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/-rr0kHlTgnh4/U4TS-UCwbMI/AAAAAAAAAKc/sGNPa8xDUFM/s1600/example.png>

Hi.

here is a simple example that shows how to select a dataset and subsequently how to populate an input selector with the column names from the selected dataset. The key is to use renderUI  <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/renderUI.html>to construct the input selector, which is not in the ui.r script, but lives in the server.r script. To see more examples on how specific elements fit together please see the Shiny gallery <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/>.

###
### ui.r
###

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

    fluidRow(
      br(),
      h1("simple dynamic selector example")
    ),
    fluidRow(
      column(2,
        selectInput("dataset", "Choose a dataset:", choices = c("rock", "pressure", "cars")),
        uiOutput("ColumnSelector")
      ),
      column(2,
        verbatimTextOutput("summary")
      )
    )
  )
)

###
### server.r
###

library(shiny)
library(datasets)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  datasetInput <- reactive({
    switch(input$dataset,
           "rock" = rock,
           "pressure" = pressure,
           "cars" = cars)
  })

  output$ColumnSelector <- renderUI({
    selectInput("SelectedColumn","select a column", choices = colnames(datasetInput()))
  })

  output$summary <- renderPrint({
    dataset <- datasetInput()
    summary(dataset[input$SelectedColumn])
  })
})

messages.body_plain:
<https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-KuXF1gzX7_I/U4ToaLsyXnI/AAAAAAAAAKs/7nbkMZrWA6E/s1600/UpdateSlider.png>

Hi,

this is easily implemented using renderUI  <http://shiny.rstudio.com/reference/shiny/latest/renderUI.html>(see my previous post).

See below for a small example that does what you want. If you press the update slider button a new slider is generated, with different end points and a different value somewhere between the minimum and maximum value (at random).

best Herman Sontrop

###
### ui.r
###

library(shiny)

shinyUI(fluidPage(

    fluidRow(
      br(),
      h1("update slider example")
    ),
    fluidRow(
      column(2,
        uiOutput("mSlider"),
        actionButton(inputId = "updateSlider", "update slider")
      )
    )
  )
)

###
### server.r
###

library(shiny)
library(datasets)

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$mSlider <- renderUI({

   #take a dependency on the action button
    input$updateSlider

    #generate a random range
    Range  <- sample(1:100)[1:2]

    #pick a random point somewhere in between
    Lambda <- runif(1)
    Value  <- Lambda*Range[1] + (1-Lambda)*(Range[2])

    #generate the slider
    sliderInput("mInput",label = "slider input",min = min(Range), max = max(Range), value =Value )
  })

})

    ),

    mainPanel(plotOutput("plot"))
  )

## server.R
###########

library(shiny)
library(zoo)

#----------------#

### build two zoo series

x1 <- c(38.2, 18.1, 83.2, 42.7, 22.8, 48.1, 81.8, 129.6, 52.0, 110.3)
x2 <- c(2.2, 0.8, 0.7, 1.6, 0.9, 0.9, 1.1, 2.8, 5.1, 2.1)

z1 <- zooreg(x1, start=as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 00:00:01"), frequency=0.0000006)
z2 <- zooreg(x2, start=as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 00:00:20"), frequency=0.0000006)
zt <- zooreg(rnorm(1050), start=as.POSIXct("2013-01-01 00:00:01"), frequency=0.00007)

z<-merge(zt, z1, all = TRUE)
z<-merge(z, z2, all = TRUE)
Zf<-na.spline(z[,2:3], na.rm = FALSE)

#startdate<-as.POSIXct("2013-03-17 00:00:01")
#enddate<-as.POSIXct("2013-03-21 23:59:59")

#----------------#

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  output$mSlider <- renderUI({

    #generate the slider
    sliderInput("mInput",label = "slider input",min = as.numeric(as.POSIXct(paste(as.character(input$dates[1])," 00:00:01", sep=""))), max = as.numeric(as.POSIXct(paste(as.character(input$dates[2])," 00:00:00", sep=""))), value =c(as.numeric(as.POSIXct(paste(as.character(input$dates[1])," 00:00:01", sep=""))), as.numeric(as.POSIXct(paste(as.character(input$dates[2])," 00:00:00", sep="")))) )
  })

  output$plot <- renderPlot({

    startdate<-as.POSIXct(input$mslider[1],origin="1970-01-01",tz="CET")
    enddate<-as.POSIXct(input$mslider[2],origin="1970-01-01",tz="CET")

    Zfw<-window(Zf, start=startdate, end=enddate)

    data1 <- switch(input$var1,
                    "wind" = Zfw$z1,
                    "waves" = Zfw$z2,
    )
    #data1<-Zfw$z1

    data2 <- switch(input$var2,
                    "wind" = Zfw$z1,
                    "waves" = Zfw$z2,
    )
    #data2<-Zfw$z2

    col1 <- switch(input$var1,
                   "wind" = "#e41a1c",
                   "waves" = "#377eb8",
    )
    #col1<-"#e41a1c"

    col2 <- switch(input$var2,
                   "wind" = "#e41a1c",
                   "waves" = "#377eb8",
    )
    #col2<-"#377eb8"

    ylab1 <- switch(input$var1,
                    "wind" = "wind speed [km/h]",
                    "waves" = "wave height [m]",
    )
    #ylab1<-"wind speed [km/h]"

    ylab2 <- switch(input$var1,
                    "wind" = "wind speed [km/h]",
                    "waves" = "wave height [m]",
    )
    #ylab2<-"wave height [m]"

    maintxt<-paste("windspeed and wave height at Dreamcoast from ", startdate, " to ", enddate, sep="")

    lnames<-c(as.character(input$var1),as.character(input$var2))
    #lnames<-c("wind", "waves")
    lcols<-c(col1,col2)

    plot(data1, col=col1 , ylim=c(0,signif(max(na.omit(data1)*1.05),2)), xlab="", ylab=ylab1,  main=maintxt)
    #grid(col = "lightgray", lty = "dotted")

    ## rightside y-axis
    opar <- par(usr = c(par("usr")[1:2], c(0,signif(max(na.omit(data2)*1.05),2))))
    axis(side = 4)
    mtext(ylab2, side = 4, line = 3, cex=0.7)

})

messages.subject: Re: Debug output in Shiny Server
messages.subject_clean: Debug output in Shiny Server
messages.body_plain:
It's not great but I usually do something like this:

cat(..., file=stderr())

You'll then have to track down the log file where the application is sending its standard-error. In a stock shiny server deployment I believe this is in /var/log/shiny-server. Each R process gets a different file. (If an R process exits gracefully, its log file is automatically deleted; if it exits with a non-zero exit code then the log file is kept.)

You can do "tail -f path-to-logfile" on the server to see the output in realtime.

It would probably be a good idea to make it very simple to log to the JavaScript console though. Maybe like a session$log().

messages.subject: Re: Difference between Shiny Server Open Source and shiny package
messages.subject_clean: Difference between Shiny Server Open Source and shiny package
messages.body_plain:
1) Each R.exe process can only host a single Shiny app, and each port can only be used by a single R process. So you'd need 10 different ports, one for each Shiny app. Shiny Server on the other hand can host multiple apps on the same port.

2) If the R.exe process terminates abnormally (e.g. an error at the wrong time) then your app will be down until you restart it. Shiny Server knows when apps go down and can bring them back up the next time someone tries to connect.

3) IE8 and 9 don't work with Shiny at all unless you have Shiny Server. This is because Shiny uses websockets to communicate with the browser, which IE didn't support until IE10. Shiny Server bridges the gap using older technologies to emulate websockets.

By the way, even when using Shiny Server, you still need R and the Shiny package installed on the server. Think of Shiny Server as a layer above the multiple R processes; it starts and stops these R processes and routes traffic to them, but doesn't replace them.

messages.subject: Re: Vector modification
messages.subject_clean: Vector modification
messages.body_plain:
Hi again,

the function isolate was used to prevent Shiny from calling renderText before you press the action button. Note that renderText depends on the values object, which is a reactiveValues object. This means that as soon as the reactiveValues object changes e.g. you append some text to the existing vector, renderText wants to execute. However, in your case you wanted to update the vector only after the string is entered completely and you press the action button. Isolate allows you to fetch a value, without creating a reactive context. In this case, it prevents a message send to renderText that it's output should be rendered.

Also note that values is a (reactiveValues) object that must be initialized and updated (in your case by pressing the button, which leads to the observe statement appending text to values$vect. Just remember, if you want to append to an object which depends on a reactive object you should consider to use a reactiveValues object.

At the start concepts like isolate, observe and reactiveValues can be a bit confusing. Don't worry, if you play around with the examples (see here <http://shiny.rstudio.com/gallery/>) you will get a good idea on how to approach things. Obviously this requires some experimentation and effort, but you will understand it for sure with some practice.

best Herman

messages.subject: Re: are there any color pickers available for Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: are there any color pickers available for Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
the code in shinysky is still there I noticed (perhaps installing shinysky on my machine had some issues)

After placing the shinysky code at github <https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky> in the www directory of my Shiny app and inserting this:

jscolorInput <- function(id) {
  tagList(
    singleton(tags$head(tags$script(src = "shinysky/inst/www/ss-jscolor.js"))),
    singleton(tags$head(tags$script(src = "shinysky/inst/www/jscolor/jscolor.js"))),
    tags$input(id = id, class = "color shiny-bound-input", onchange = sprintf("$('#%s').trigger('afterChange')",id)),
    tags$script(sprintf("$('#%s').trigger('afterChange')",id))
  )
}

at the top of the ui.r script the color picker appears (shinysky in the code block above is a folder in my www directory holding the github code of shinysky).

The color picker then can and used by including jscolorInput("myColorPicker") somewhere in the ui.r script. The color value can subsequently be accessed by input$myColorPicker.

Still curious if alternative schemes exist though...

best Herman
